title: Audit workflow security
prompt: Review permissions, action references, secrets, expression handling, and trust boundaries.
objective: Demonstrate the behavior of audit workflow security and capture verifiable evidence.

starter.code:
name: Harden a validation workflow
on: [push, pull_request]
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: validation-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - run: echo "Run non-privileged checks"

expected_output: A reviewed workflow or design note satisfying: permissions:, secrets, pull_request_target. Verify behavior on a disposable repository where execution is required; a static sketch is not proof of a live deployment.
acceptance_criteria: Explain one validation result or limitation.
Do not include a real secret or use production resources.
hints: First identify the trigger, input, and expected result.
Start with read-only permissions and a disposable branch or test environment.
Compare your result with the linked lesson and official documentation; distinguish a configuration sketch from a live integration.

solution.explanation: The detailed reference solution is stored in a protected repository-only JSON file; it is not intended for a learner-facing response.

grading_method: Server-side required-string smoke check plus human review for workflow semantics and security boundaries.
retry_policy: Allow retries; incorrect submissions do not award XP. The platform awards exercise XP only after server-verified successful completion and applies idempotency per activity.
status_note: Source mapping: Section C: Practical Exercises; original learning task adapted to CodeLeaf structure. Starter example aligned with its linked lesson; review and replace any remaining repository-specific placeholders.
